title: Unsafe Property Access error ignores type check
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.arch_linux [ed1daf0bf], v4.8.dev5.official [9552dfb68]

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable (ed1daf0bf) - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue, 08 Sep 2026 10:22:31 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (nvidia; 615.71.09) - AMD Ryzen 5 2600 Six-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.28 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When `debug/gdscript/warnings/unsafe_property_access` and `debug/gdscript/warnings/unsafe_method_access` warnings are set to warning or error, they produce errors even in a type checked block.

I have three classes:
```
extends Resource
class_name Reward
````
```
extends Reward
class_name GoldReward

@export var value: int

func calc() -> int:
	return 2 * value
```
```
extends Node2D

func foo(reward: Reward) -> void:
	if reward is GoldReward: # Type check
		print(reward.value) # Error from unsafe property access
		print(reward.calc()) # Error from unsafe method access

func _ready() -> void:
	var gold_reward: GoldReward = GoldReward.new()
	foo(gold_reward)
```

I think that if a variable has been type checked, then the inferred type of that variable should be changed for that block, so that those lines wouldn't cause errors.

Those errors are useful for moments where I forget a type check and am notified of that (that's why I turn them on), but are annoying if after the type check I still get them.

Current workaround is to also have `as`:
```
print((reward as GoldReward).value)
print((reward as GoldReward).calc())
```
But this is annoying. The parser (? not sure if this is where errors are found) has the information to know that those accesses are legal, because an explicit type check was made, so why can't it just... not throw the errors? :D

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open MRP
2. Observer errors
